title: Seven - No, Wait, Five - Mysteries of the Art World
summary: Josh and Chuck count down a "top five" style list of art world mysteries (the show jokes about its old House Stuff Works top-ten lists). Topics: Caravaggio's murder of Ramuccio Tomassoni, his flight to Malta, the Knights of Malta, and the ambiguous "F" signature in the Beheading of John the Baptist; Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring, its unknown sitter and changing titles; Raphael's stolen Portrait of a Young Man from the Czartoryski Museum taken by the Nazis under Hans Frank; Van Gogh's 1890 death and the theory he was accidentally shot by teenager Gachet/Secrétan boys; and Hitler's rejected art career and the market for forged Hitler watercolors. Also a mention of the Gardner Museum heist as a future episode topic, and a listener mail segment about using middle names (Amy, whose first name is Helen).

segments.title: Opening banter and list format
segments.summary: Hosts welcome listeners, joke about a missed welcome line, and discuss the show's old top-ten lists and this seven-item-turned-five list. They chat about the Fast and Furious films.

segments.title: Caravaggio
segments.summary: Caravaggio's violent life: killing Ramuccio Tomassoni, fleeing to Malta, briefly joining the Knights of Malta, and painting the Beheading of John the Baptist. They discuss his signature in blood with the ambiguous 'F', theories about its meaning, his expulsion from the Order, and his death in Tuscany.

segments.title: Vermeer and Girl with a Pearl Earring
segments.summary: Vermeer's career and family life, the unidentified sitter of Girl with a Pearl Earring and its many earlier titles, the speculation about his daughter Maria, the Tracy Chevalier novel and film, and the painting's technique. A documentary about Vermeer's methods is mentioned.

segments.title: Raphael's missing Portrait of a Young Man
segments.summary: The Czartoryski Museum's three key paintings, their seizure by the Nazis and placement with Hans Frank, the recovery of two of them, and the disappearance of Raphael's Portrait of a Young Man. Its appearance in The Simpsons and the 2016 purchase of the collection with the empty frame are noted.

segments.title: Transition to Van Gogh
segments.summary: Brief pronunciation banter about Van Gogh's name, referencing a Woody Allen film.

segments.title: Van Gogh's death
segments.summary: Van Gogh's ear cutting and his 1890 death at 37. Authors Steven Naifeh and Gregory White Smith's 2011 book argues he was accidentally shot by teenage boys, René Secrétan and his brother, with a gun that misfired. Circumstantial evidence, Secrétan's later admission that it was his gun, and Van Gogh's final words are discussed. Chuck and Josh also mention an immersive Van Gogh exhibit in Atlanta.

segments.title: Hitler's paintings and forgeries
segments.summary: Hitler's rejection by the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts, his selling of copied postcard watercolors in Vienna and Munich, his failed military physical, his service in World War One, and the destruction of his works. Critics' views of his art, and the market for forged Hitler watercolors, including auction sales in 2009 and 2015, are discussed.

segments.title: Closing mentions: Gardner Museum heist
segments.summary: Josh says a future episode on the Gardner Museum heist is planned, since it was on the list but underplayed.

segments.title: Listener mail: middle names
segments.summary: Listener Amy writes that her family uses middle names, so she goes by Amy though her first name is Helen, which confuses airports and doctors. The hosts read it and thank her.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address and iHeartRadio credit.
